name: Swim Technique
description: Freestyle technique with no schedule. Pick whatever you feel like when you get to the pool: the full session is the default, and the drill blocks are there to grab on their own.
creator: WOD

schedule.label: Full Session
schedule.notes: Kick drills, rotation drills, then swim. The default.

schedule.label: Kick Drills
schedule.notes: Wall kick and kick on your back. Grab these whenever the legs are the thing.

schedule.label: Rotation Drills
schedule.notes: Side-kick drill and 6-3-6. Grab these whenever the roll or the breathing is the thing.

tips: No schedule — pick whatever you feel like.
Drills go first, while you're fresh. A drill done tired grooves the bad version.
Rest at the wall until your breathing settles, however long that takes.
Stroke count on a full-stroke length is the only number worth having. Not laps, not time.

overview.goal: Better freestyle: breathing, rotation, kick. Not speed, not distance.
overview.whatToExpect: One problem at a time, in order. Each stage gets its own drill block, and the next starts once the last one feels natural. The full session always runs the same shape: warm up, drills while you're fresh, then swim with one thing to think about.
keyPrinciples: 1. Rotation — roll your whole body side to side so you breathe off the roll instead of craning your neck.
2. Kick — small and loose, swinging from the hip joint.
3. Catch — how your hand grabs the water. Where lifting strength finally helps.
4. Rhythm — breathing pattern and kick timing.
